title: GameCube and Wii: our own emulator, written from scratch in Rust (owner, 23 October 2026)
replaces: The old Dolphin plan (GC1 to GC5, Dolphin plus our interpreter) is replaced and must not be followed; it is in git history.

owner_answers_23_october.wii: Plan Wii in from the start (same emulator, GameCube first).
owner_answers_23_october.reading: Anything may be read to learn how the hardware works, Dolphin's source included, as long as nobody has to be credited. So: read, understand, write our own; never copy code, tables or files (Dolphin's per-game settings database, fonts, etc. are theirs: make our own).
owner_answers_23_october.dolphin_as_yardstick: Yes: Dolphin may run on the test machine only, to compare results (like MAME for cArcade). Never in the app, never committed except our own recorded reference results.
owner_answers_23_october.libraries: Owner, 23 October (correcting an earlier reading): ANY libraries may be used (serde, bincode, a code generator and so on). What is not allowed is a FULL emulator core by someone else (Dolphin or any other GameCube/Wii emulator, or a wrapper of one). Libraries keep their small notices in the credits list; that is fine.
owner_answers_23_october.name: Working name continuum-gc (crate continuum_gc, option prefix cgc_). Owner: do not ask about the name; pick and carry on. A player-facing name can be set later; the option keys are only fixed once it ships.
owner_answers_23_october.first_build: No build until real games play properly. Until then no phone build for this work.
owner_answers_23_october.jit_testers: The owner knows nobody with JIT. The JIT is proved on the test machine only (ARM64 under an emulator such as qemu-user).
owner_answers_23_october.best_cpu_24_october: Owner, 24 October 2026, about 6:50 AM Eastern: 'I want the absolute best... best fast interpreter, best JIT, better than Dolphin... I don't care how long it takes.' So G7 is a pre-decoded, threaded interpreter (operands decoded once, one small handler per instruction form, direct RAM access through the translation cache, time and interrupt checks per block, block linking, idle-loop skipping), proved identical to the plain interpreter (examples/compare.rs and per-instruction fuzz tests); G8 is a full ARM64 JIT with register allocation, fast memory, block linking and the same idle skipping. Aim: faster than Dolphin's interpreter and JIT on the same phone.
owner_answers_23_october.evidence_24_october: Owner, 24 October 2026, about 7 AM Eastern, two screenshots (they reach the chat only, not the disk, so they could not be saved as files): Manic EMU on his iPhone 17 Pro Max, no JIT, CPU Emulation Method set to 'Cached Interpreter (slower)' (Dolphin's cached interpreter), playing Star Wars Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike in game (the Mos Eisley hangar level with the radar and timer), 'basically perfect, barely any hiccups', better than Manic's own 'Manic Interpreter (experimental)'. So the bar for our no-JIT path: at least Dolphin's cached-interpreter speed on that phone, plus a GPU drawer (Dolphin draws on the GPU; our CPU drawer alone cannot carry such games on a phone).
owner_answers_23_october.experimental_builds_24_october: Owner, 24 October 2026, about 7:40 AM Eastern: 'I don't mind testing [an] experimental GC build ... but I don't want to constantly have to do that. Idk.' So: occasional experimental GameCube builds are fine, NOT one per change. Plan: at most one experimental build at a big milestone (first time: the core wired into the app as an opt-in experimental GameCube core, with disc/ISO loading, memory cards, the fast interpreter; it will be slow without the GPU drawer and silent in games without the AX sound stand-in). Offer it once in a report with clear test steps; start it only when he says yes. This replaces 'no build until real games play' only for these rare opt-in test builds. Build 214 was that build (the owner chose the hidden unlock, B); it failed on GitHub's side while uploading, so 215 replaced it (started 1:42 PM with the memory card and the controls fix). After it, GameCube rides along in normal builds; no separate GameCube builds.

hard_rules: Own crate in cores/ like cores/continuum-gb and cores/continuum-arcade, a libretro cdylib built by scripts/build-core.sh as an OPTIONAL core.
No other emulator's code in the core (no Dolphin, no wrapper). Ordinary libraries are fine.

JIT: our own ARM64 code generator, used automatically when crates/emulator-bridge/src/jit.rs says yes (GET_JIT_CAPABLE at load, code memory through continuum_jit_region on TXM phones, core id added to core_may_use_jit). Never required.
A fast interpreter for phones without JIT (the owner's iPhone 17 Pro Max), proved identical to the plain interpreter.
Settings: every setting any current GameCube/Wii emulator offers, and more (docs/CORE_OPTIONS_STANDARD.md). The list is made FIRST, generated from source.
Test only with homebrew, our own test programs and free content. Never fetch a commercial game, BIOS (IPL) or Wii keys.
No boot picture unless the player's own real IPL file is present.

steps.title: Reading games: DOL/ELF homebrew, ISO/GCM, then RVZ, GCZ, CISO, WIA, WBFS with our own decompressors; direct boot without an IPL
steps.progress: Done so far: DOL and ELF loader (src/dol.rs), plain ISO/GCM reader and disc header/apploader (src/disc.rs), IPL-free boot: DOL direct, disc via the disc's own apploader run on our CPU (src/machine.rs boot_disc). Left: RVZ, WIA, GCZ, CISO, WBFS; Wii discs (partitions, decryption). | 24 October afternoon: commercial discs refused in build 216 (owner, Animal Crossing .nkit.iso and .rvz): the apploader faulted because r13/r2 were 0. Disc boot now gives the boot ROM's r1/r2/r13 (NTSC/PAL) and exactly Dolphin's boot-ROM low memory (devkit console type 0x10000006, rfi at 0x300/0x800/0xC00, identity post-matrices, no arena/bi2/FST presets). Refusals reach the screen ('cGC:' log line, engine passes it on); a game showing nothing for 15 s gets a status screen (notice.rs). Build 219 carries it.

steps.title: Correct plain interpreter of the Gekko/Broadway CPU (PowerPC 750 plus paired singles), MMU/BATs, exceptions, timers, proved by test programs
steps.progress: Plain interpreter written (src/cpu/: mod.rs registers/SPRs/exceptions/memory, interp.rs integer/branch/load-store/system, fpu.rs FP and paired singles, mmu.rs BATs + hashed page table). 26 CPU tests pass. Known gaps (fpu.rs header): fres/frsqrte exact instead of the hardware estimate tables, rounding modes only in fctiw, approximate XX/OX/UX flags, FP-enabled exceptions not raised. Next: check against a public PowerPC test suite and against Dolphin as yardstick (owner allowed, test machine only). Speed on the x86 sandbox: ~179 MIPS (examples/speed.rs).

steps.title: Rest of the console: memory map, interrupts, VI, PI, DI, EXI (memory cards, RTC), SI (pads, rumble), AI, ARAM, DSP (our own HLE of the common sound microcodes)
steps.progress: Started (src/hw.rs): PI interrupts, VI registers/display interrupts/timing and the YUV framebuffer picture, SI controllers (status, origin, polling), EXI clock/SRAM/UART chip, DI read/inquiry, DSP mailbox (reset mail 0x8071FEED, mails acknowledged) and ARAM DMA, AI registers. Left: real DSP sound (our own stand-ins for the sound programs), audio DMA output, memory cards, CP/PE (with G6), exact timing, Wii Hollywood/IOS. 24 October: PI bus-error bit (programs use it to tell GameCube from Wii), the CPU's thermal unit, UART fixed (whole lines), VI line stride fixed (32-byte units), SD card adapter on serial port 2 (src/sd.rs, SPI protocol, SDHC, read/write; dev runner CGC_SD=image), loader-style argv/envp (Machine::set_args; dev CGC_ARGV/CGC_ENV). | 24 October afternoon: AX (dsp_ax.rs) and the Zelda family (dsp_zelda.rs) stand-ins; memory card in slot A (memcard.rs, see G9); SI polling with RDST/NOREP/RDSTINT (controls never reached games before 3394ad4); EXI wire time and 64-byte register mirror; RTC from the phone's local time, ticking, time base from it; SRAM language/flags order and flash ID checksums fixed; Japanese discs set VI DTV bit 1. Left: DTK disc-streamed music (DI E1/E2), IPL font replacement, PAL (0xCC and 50 Hz), exact DI timing. | Also from reading Animal Crossing's SDK code (ac-decomp, reading only): drive commands now take two video lines (an instant completion beat the library's 10 s timeout, which then masked the drive interrupt); nothing answers past 16 MB of ARAM (wrapping made the OS find 4 MB of expansion); OSInit's audio start-up and ARInit's size check replayed in tests. | 24 October evening (after build 219, Animal Crossing stuck in __AI_SRC_INIT): the AI sample counter counts from the CPU's clock sample by sample (54 MHz / 1124 or / 1686; Hw::ai_sync, re-anchored on AICR/AISCNT writes; AIINT when it reaches AIIT); every register access knows the CPU's time (Cpu::now: cycles plus the running block's or JIT chain's instructions, Bus::clock); the check replayed as a PowerPC program passes on plain, fast and JIT. Animal Crossing's own sound program (jdsp in ac-decomp dspboot.c, Ector 0x4BE6A5CB) read from its jump table at 0x0062: command 0B takes one word (fixed; 0C already did), command 2 waits for one zero mail per subframe and raises DSPINT after its voices (as modelled); its whole start-up (MXIC boot, hello, DwaitFrame, DsetupTable, DiplSec, frames of 7 subframes) is replayed in tests.

steps.title: Graphics: exact CPU drawer as yardstick, then a GPU drawer through the engine's Vulkan path
steps.progress: 24 October, first pass done (src/gx/): CP FIFO (PI write-gather bursts, linked FIFO, watermarks, breakpoints, display lists), CP/XF/BP registers, vertex loader (all formats, direct/indexed, NBT), XF transform with projection, lighting (diffuse, spot, specular attenuation), texgen (2x4/3x4, emboss, colour, dual-tex post matrices), clipping, culling, exact edge-function rasteriser (1/16 px, top-left rule), perspective-correct attributes and LOD, TEV (16 stages, konst, swap tables, compare modes, indirect texturing), alpha test, fog, z textures, textures (I4/I8/IA4/IA8/565/5A3/RGBA8/C4/C8/C14X2/CMPR, TLUT, preload, mipmaps, bilinear), PE (z, blend, logic op, formats), EFB copies to XFB (YUV, gamma, y-scale, copy filter, interlace) and to textures (all formats, box filter), EFB peek/poke, PE token/finish and CP interrupts. Checked on the test machine: FCE Ultra GX menu, Swiss home screen and Neverball's 3D title all draw correctly (pictures in .kiro/notes/docs/gamecube/). Left: exact TEV rounding vs hardware, line/point texture offsets, bounding box, Z16 formats, AA, speed (CPU drawer ~6 fields/s with the plain interpreter), then the GPU drawer. Speed, 24 October (all proved to draw exactly the same with examples/drawcheck.rs, which records per-field fingerprints of the colour buffer, depth buffer and picture): texture wrap without division, mip levels scaled by exact reciprocals, textures decoded a block at a time (test: every block format vs texel-by-texel), and pixels drawn on helper threads (src/gx/draw.rs: interleaved 8-row bands, every primitive in order, EFB copies/clears/CPU access/save states wait first). Neverball 1.8x quicker overall, FCE Ultra GX 2.5x; the core uses all cores but two, at most four. Measured on the test machine: about 90 ns a pixel per thread (TEV interpretation, texture sampling, blending); still to do: per-stage TEV operand plans, then the GPU drawer.

steps.title: Fast interpreter (no-JIT phones), proved identical to G4, speed measured
steps.progress: 24 October: src/cpu/fast.rs + fast_ops.rs: instructions decoded once into handlers, blocks per physical page, chained in one call, linked (two remembered targets per block), exact idle-loop fast-forward, FP quick path, translation cache kept across exceptions, data-window memory shortcut (first DBAT, two compares). Proved identical: fuzz test (3 million random instructions vs the plain interpreter), FP quick-path test (4 million operands), examples/compare.rs on all three programs. Speed (x86 test machine): simple loop 274 vs plain 97 million instructions a second. Measured with examples/hot.rs on Neverball: loads/stores 32% of instructions (99% inside the data window), register jumps 2.9% (the two remembered targets hit 95%, a return stack would reach 100%), commonest neighbouring pair only 3.5% (compare+branch family 7%), memcpy about 5%, nothing else stands out. So fused instruction pairs (about 1%), a return stack (under 0.5%) and host replacements for memcpy and friends are not worth it now; guaranteed tail calls are not in stable Rust (tested, 1.92: 'become' is experimental). Left: dedicated paired-single and psq handlers.

steps.title: Our own ARM64 JIT through jit.rs, proved identical on the test machine
steps.progress: 24 October: src/jit/: a64.rs (ARM64 encoder, checked against LLVM), compile.rs (block compiler: integer, compare, rotate, load/store with an inline main-memory path inside the data BAT window, branches; every other instruction calls the fast interpreter's own handler), runtime.rs (compiled after two runs, blocks linked straight into each other, blr/bctr through a 64K-entry lookup table, unlinked when code changes, all reset when the area fills or the BAT mapping changes), native.rs (iPhone code memory from the app's continuum_jit_region, two addresses; mmap on ARM64 Linux), unicorn.rs (feature 'unicorn': runs the code in an ARM64 emulator on x86). Turned on at load when the app says JIT is allowed. Proved: 20,000 random blocks (with chaining, short budgets and table jumps) equal to the handlers, through Unicorn and as real ARM64 code under qemu-aarch64 (.scratch/ca cargo wrapper); examples/compare.rs plain vs JIT IDENTICAL on Swiss (150 fields), FCE Ultra GX (150) and Neverball (200), and drawcheck with JIT plus 3 drawing threads draws exactly the same. Neverball: 99.7% of instructions run in compiled code; simple loop under qemu: JIT 497 vs fast 25 million instructions a second. Left: register cache, floating point and paired singles native, real-mode (translation off) blocks, measured on the phone.

steps.title: Saves and controls: memory cards, save states, GameCube touch layout, rumble
steps.progress: 24 October: memory card done (memcard.rs): 251 blocks, slot A, the game's SAVE_RAM (.srm per game), blank cards formatted like the library, any card image mounts (SRAM gets the card's flash ID), save states keep only the card's command state. Proved with GCMM (restore, list after restart, format) and unit tests through the EXI registers. Save states: work (layout CGC3, older ones refused with a reason). Touch layout: GameCube pad in TouchControls. Left: rumble check on a game, slot B, 59/1019-block card images (only 2 MB images fit now).
